sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cold-Chain Keg Wholesale and Export of Artisanal Hazy IPAs

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy of Luxembourg) - unitary national jurisdiction without sub-state tax differentiation
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Code Civil and Code de Commerce of Napoleonic derivation, substantially harmonised with EU corporate, tax and AML/CFT law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation, signed 3 April 1996, as amended by the Protocol of 20 May 2009
Luxembourg-Germany Double Taxation Agreement of 8 August 1989, as amended by the Protocol of 9 November 2012
Luxembourg-France Double Taxation Agreement of 1 April 1958, as amended by successive protocols
Luxembourg-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement of 24 May 1967, as amended
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since 21 September 2017
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 49 and 54 (freedom of establishment for companies)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Laws of 10 August 2018, 25 March 2020 and 7 July 2022 (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law) and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 March 2019; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the SCSp regime into Article 902-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Partnership Agreement (contrat de societe) of the SCSp, including subscription undertakings of the general and limited partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg civil-law notary for the notarial form; otherwise executed as a private deed executed by the general partner and limited partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for notarial acts executed outside Luxembourg; Consular Legalization for jurisdictions not party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incorporation (extrait du registre) of each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or Chamber of Commerce of the partner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the designated competent authority of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (procuration) for the incorporation signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the jurisdiction where the appointing partner is located
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization where the origin jurisdiction is outside the Hague Apostille network

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports or national identity documents of all beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant national identity authority; certification by a Luxembourg notary or by a consular official of the holder's nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the certifying notarial or consular certificate; sworn French translation required where the document is not issued in French, German, Luxembourgish or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered office and domiciliation acceptance letter (attestation de domiciliation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Approved domiciliation agent or professional of the financial sector (PSF) in Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; original signed letter submitted by the domiciliation agent directly to the RCS in the incorporation file

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under Articles 3 and 5 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, as amended: (i) PEP screening is compulsory for all beneficial owners, directors, general partners and authorised signatories, including family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence (EDD) and mandatory source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification for any PEP relationship; (ii) automated screening against the consolidated EU asset-freeze lists (Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and Regulation (EU) No 833/2014, as implemented by Grand-Ducal regulations), the UN Security Council sanctions lists, and, on a risk-based supplemental basis for USD transactions, the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists; (iii) screening is required at pre-incorporation KYC, at onboarding and continuously through transaction monitoring in accordance with CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, Chapter 7; (iv) any positive match or suspicious activity must be reported without delay to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier - CRF), with strict prohibition of tipping-off; (v) the RBE declaration must identify every beneficial owner holding more than 25% of the partnership interests or voting rights, and the relevance threshold applies to the economic substance of the SCSp rather than to its nominal capital.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), official portal https://www.lbr.lu, with e-filing and name-search modules accessible also through the single government procedure at https://guichet.lu.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filings and the company name itself must be expressed in French, Luxembourgish, German or English, entered in Latin script. A non-Latin name must be transliterated into Latin characters, and that transliteration must be used consistently in the deed, the RESA publication and the RBE file. The statutory legal-form identifier must appear at the end of the name, either as 'SCSp' or as 'societe en commandite speciale' spelled out; the use of any other legal-form suffix is rejected by the RCS as misleading.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Letzebuerg (requires prior authorization from the Ministry of Economy)
Versicherung (requires prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
fonds d'investissement (requires prior CSSF authorization for fund activity)
Chambre des Metiers (reserved to the statutory chambers)
SARL (legal-form tokens that must correspond exactly to the adopted legal form and cannot be used for an SCSp)
Ltd and any foreign legal-form suffix (rejected as misleading for the RCS)
Etat du Luxembourg and official state symbols (prohibited)

stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Reservation: the applicant files a name-reservation and non-opposition request with the RCS Registrar through the LBR portal; the Registrar issues an electronic clearance certificate once the availability search confirms that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing reservation or registered entry. Validity: 30 calendar days from the date of clearance, renewable twice upon reasoned request and payment of the renewal tariff, for a maximum cumulative period of 90 days. Rejection and appeal: (1) the Registrar must issue a reasoned refusal; (2) within 8 calendar days of notification, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar through the LBR e-file; (3) if the refusal is upheld, a formal administrative appeal must be lodged with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber) within 40 calendar days of notification of the decision; (4) concurrently, a hierarchical appeal may be addressed to the Minister of Justice within 15 calendar days, and any final ministerial or registral decision remains subject to judicial review before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within 3 months of notification; (5) the appeal must be drafted in French or accompanied by a sworn French translation, and the applicant may simultaneously request a new reservation under a modified or differently transliterated name to protect the incorporation timetable.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Part II on limited partnerships); Law of 12 July 2013 on Alternative Investment Funds (SCSp regime); Grand-Ducal Regulation on the Commercial Register of 23 January 2003
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCSL) — Luxembourg Business Registers, R.C.S. Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement / Articles of Association (Contrat de Société) drawn up by private deed, with electronic filing via the RCSL eJustice portal (eProcurement/LFSS)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; SCSp may be established with zero capital. Contributions may be cash or in kind, without statutory minimum, and if contributed must be placed in an escrow or partnership corporate bank account subject to AML/KYC verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the sole general partner of LU_SCSp (Special Limited Partnership), and the special partners executing this resolution, hereby unanimously resolve as follows: (1) The partnership capital shall be subscribed as set forth in the articles of association; no minimum paid-up capital is required and any contribution may be held on escrow or the partnership's corporate bank account as identified by the manager. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. (3) [Name] and [Name] are appointed as gérants/managers with sole and unrestricted power to bind the partnership. (4) The RCSL filing of the articles and the appointment formalities are approved and delegated. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL (electronic platform) and any professional adviser (notary or duly appointed local counsel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect and verify the identity, residential address, and power of attorney of the general partner, special partners, and designated managers. Carry out AML/KYC checks; obtain certified copies of passports, and where relevant, extract from partnership register. Determine whether the registered office will be provided by the general partner, a leased office, or a service provider, and obtain landlord or provider consent.
required_dossiers: Certified passports (general and special partners, managers)
Proof of residential address (individuals) or extract from corporate register (entities)
Power of attorney for signing partner if not the general partner
Draft partnership agreement / articles of association
Registered office consent agreement from landlord or service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any identification document is expired or insufficiently clear, resubmit certified copies or apostilled documents within 5 business days; if the proposed registered office is refused by the building manager, appoint a new registered office address and resubmit consent form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of partnership agreement and adoption of corporate governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner and all special partners; private deed signed before a public notary only if notarial act is required under the partnership agreement or due to in-kind contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize and sign the partnership agreement (acte de société) in one original counterpart. The agreement shall state the firm name, registered office, corporate purpose (craft beer wholesale, distribution, and export of craft beers, including hazy IPAs under ISIC 4632), duration, management powers, capital structure, and special partner limitation of liability. Simultaneously adopt the pro-forma first resolution appointing the manager(s) and fixing the registered office. If any contribution is in kind, the statutory auditor or expert report must be obtained and annexed.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (original or electronic with advanced signature)
Pro-forma first board resolution (or general meeting minutes)
Expert valuation report (for in-kind contributions, if any)
Bank certificate of capital deposit (if capital is used)
Written consent to appointment from each manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCSL or the notary queries the legality of a clause, amend the partnership agreement by private deed of ratification signed by all partners; if expert valuation report is defective, obtain a supplementary report and file with the RCSL.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCSL registration filing and request for registration number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) - eJustice filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the RCSL eJustice portal using a Luxembourg eID (Electronic Luxembourg ID) or appointed accredited representative. Upload the completed registration pack: electronic filing form, partnership agreement, first resolution, registered office consent, identification documents, and proof of payment of the filing fee. Submit the file and obtain an acknowledgment receipt with the application reference number.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration application form (form C or the electronic equivalent)
Signed partnership agreement (scanned PDF)
Pro-forma first resolution / managers' appointment
Registered office consent (notarized, if requested by RCSL)
Identity and capacity documents of partners/managers
Proof of payment of filing fees (exchange on credit or e-payment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCSL issues a query or deficiency notice, respond within one month by uploading additional explanation, corrected documents, or translations as required. If the deadline is missed, refile the application with a new fee and explain the delay to the registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the electronic official gazette (RESA) and issuance of RCSL extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL / Ministry of Justice — Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCSL approval, the RCSL automatically publishes the legal notice in the RESA gazette. Verify the contents of the RESA extract (name, registered office, partners, managers, capital, object). Retain the RCSL registration number and obtain the full RCSL extract (extrait) as the official certificate of incorporation for banking and licensing purposes.
required_dossiers: RCSL approval decision and registration number
RCSL extract (issued in due course)
Proof of RESA publication (online electronic voucher)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA notice contains erroneous data, immediately file a formal request for rectification with the RCSL, attaching the correct extract and a cover letter; the rectification is published in the next RESA edition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration statutory registrations (tax, labor, and industry) and physical licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (ACD), Registration Office (Luxembourg Administration des douanes et accises), Ministry of Health, Ministry of the Environment, Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM), and relevant communal authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCSL extract is obtained, register for VAT (if annual turnover exceeds EUR 35,000) using form 577; apply for an EORI number from the Customs and Excise Administration for cross-border distribution; register the partnership with the Chamber of Commerce and National Social Security (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale) for employee payroll; apply for the business establishment authorisation and food business approval (if applicable). For environmental matters, file a category 3 preliminary declaration with the competent administration if the storage/warehouse facility is covered by the classification list.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration extract (original)
Partnership agreement (signed)
Identification of managers and partners
Registered office lease / service provider contract
Food business emergency and safety plan (for distribution storage)
Environmental class declaration form and racking plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Health or ITM issues a deficiency, provide the requested heat, hygiene, structural load, or fire-safety documentation within the stated period (usually 10 business days). If environmental classification is deemed higher than declared, file a full class application and pay the corrected fee; never begin operations before receipt of definitive approvals.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy of Luxembourg (Direction de la Qualité et de la Sécurité) jointly with the Ministry of Health (Food Safety Directorate) for alimentary business registration; communal authorities for commercial establishment licence
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit - IB category for alcoholic beverage wholesale) and Food Business Operator Registration (HC/BPF category) under Regulation (EC) 852/2004 and the Luxembourg Law of 29 May 1995

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development (Administration de l'environnement – Office of the Environment)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / simple declaration (Class 3) for a non-intensive storage and distribution warehouse (cold chain keg storage) under the amended Grand-Ducal Regulation of 16 May 2014; full EIA required only if annual production capacity of beer exceeds 300,000 hectolitres (Annex I category 7(c)).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (91/271/EEC) and the Luxembourg Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 July 2010; for any process water, limit for BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L and COD ≤ 125 mg/L. VOCs: storage and distribution operations must comply with the EU Solvent Emissions Directive (2004/42/EC) and the national regulation on VOCs (ONDV), with annual VOC emissions below 5 tonnes (no solvent management plan required). Waste: separation and recovery of spent kegs, cardboard, and glass under the Law of 21 March 2012 on Waste Management; disposal of waste oil in approved facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: obtained from the Administration de la protection contre l'incendie et les secours (APCIS) following inspection of the cold-storage and distribution warehouse; must include evacuation plan, extinguishing systems, and addressable fire-alarm. Structural load inspection: certificate from a state-accredited structural engineer for racking systems and cold-storage floors. Occupational clearance: workplace safety assessment and first-aid training verification issued by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD; Luxembourg Inland Revenue) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); filings and registrations accessible through the MyGuichet.lu portal and Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SCSp in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a notary to obtain the business registration number; request a national tax identification number (matricule) from ACD; apply separately to AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT number using Form 1000/1020, attaching the RCS extract, constitutional documents, proof of registered office, partner details, and estimated turnover. Non-resident partners may require a Luxembourg VAT number if importing or engaging in VAT-liable transactions; the SCSp may optionally register for VAT even below the EUR 35,000 threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SCSp is fiscally transparent under default rules; a partnership may elect or be treated as a taxable corporate entity under Article 175 LIR if it carries on a commercial activity in Luxembourg. Anti-hybrid rules under ATAD (implemented by Luxembourg law of 23 December 2016) restrict hybrid mismatch elections. A check-the-box-style election is not generally available; transparency is automatic unless a valid corporate-taxation election or commercial-activity trigger applies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA - taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small enterprise exemption); mandatory registration for non-established suppliers and for intra-EU distance sales exceeding EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold under the OSS; no threshold for importation or reverse-charge acquisitions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping; e-invoicing is mandatory for B2G (central government, PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format); B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary; invoice data must be retained for 6 years; no API-based fiscal clearance requirement exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to direct exports of goods from Luxembourg to non-EU destinations where the exporter retains proof that the goods left the EU within 90 days of supply, including for craft beer shipped under EXW/FOB/CIF terms; ancillary transport services and certain B2B services to non-EU customers may be zero-rated or outside scope provided business status and actual performance are documented.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD) with Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure from the EU
Commercial Invoice and Packing List conforming to customs valuation requirements
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Transport documentation and insurance certificate supporting the export supply chain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may scrutinize zero-rating claims within the 5-year statute of limitation (10 years in cases of fraud); unsubstantiated or fraudulent export claims trigger immediate reversal of zero-rating, VAT collection at 17% plus default interest at 0.8% per month, administrative fines up to EUR 250,000, and imprisonment up to 5 years for criminal fraud; in an SCSp, the general partner and certain partners may be jointly and severally liable for assessed VAT and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS registration confirmation and renewal (déclaration annuelle / renouvellement RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar rule: due during the LBR annual renewal period in the first calendar quarter; the precise invoice date is fixed by the LBR annual renewal notice and is generally by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalty on late renewal, formal reminder from the RCS, and administrative strike-off (radiation) if the renewal remains unpaid; strike-off removes the RCS entry and may interrupt the SCSp's legal capacity and bank operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar rule: by 31 March of each calendar year; ownership changes are declared within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000, public publication of the sanction, and, in case of intentional omission, imprisonment of the general partner or responsible officer.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SCSp is not subject to automatic statutory audit solely on legal form. A mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé is triggered if the SCSp meets the large-undertaking criteria (balance-sheet total above EUR 4,400,000, net turnover above EUR 8,800,000, and average headcount above 50), if consolidated accounts are prepared, or if the partnership agreement requires it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial and company registers and annual accounts, as amended); IFRS as adopted by the EU is available for voluntary presentation and is mandatory for consolidated financial statements if applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For the SCSp, the members are the general partner and the limited partners. A transfer of a partnership interest is effective against the SCSp only when recorded in the register of partners. On any transfer or change of beneficial ownership, the general partner must file an updated RBE declaration within one month. Every calendar year, by 31 March, the general partner must confirm in the RBE portal that the current list of beneficial owners of the SCSp remains accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners (general and limited partners) with contribution and transfer history
Register of beneficial owners required by the UBO Act
Minute book of partner resolutions and consents
Register of contributions, distributions, and withdrawals
Commercial and accounting ledgers if the SCSp carries on a commercial activity

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – USD 4,500 per annum for a standard Luxembourg registered-office and company-secretarial provider, including UBO annual confirmation and RCS renewal handling.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 14,000 per annum for a certified Luxembourg independent audit, where required by statutory thresholds or by the partnership agreement.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax; aggregate rate in Luxembourg City approx. 29.22%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent; no entity-level CIT. IP income may benefit from the 80% patent box exemption; investment tax credit of 8% on qualifying assets; participation exemption on qualifying dividends/capital gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Corporate Income Tax Return), Form 100A (Municipal Business Tax Return), Form 100B (Net Wealth Tax Return) filed electronically via e-Déclarations (ed.tax.lu) using a LuxTrust digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the fiscal year corresponds to the calendar year unless the partnership deed validly adopts a different accounting period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar year, the return must be filed by 31 December of the following tax year; extensions are administratively available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial register number, Luxembourg business tax matricule, and registered office details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must identify the PE and its Luxembourg tax number; otherwise state the SCSp is transparent and no Form 100 is required at entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss derived from the audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must allocate to the PE only the profit attributable to the Luxembourg craft-beer distribution activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reintegration of non-deductible expenses: entertaining, fines, excessive director remuneration, 50% of certain vehicle costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same add-backs apply; expenses booked at foreign head office cannot be deducted against Luxembourg PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward from prior years applied against current taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Luxembourg-sourced PE losses that were previously assessed may be carried forward; losses of a foreign head office are ineligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base for municipal business tax (Form 100A) before applying the municipal multiplier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Municipal business tax applies to the Luxembourg PE; foreign partners without a PE have no Luxembourg municipal business tax exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger a surcharge of up to 10% of the tax due when filed after formal notice, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%; administrative fines up to EUR 1,000 per infringement; criminal penalties apply in cases of wilful late filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding tax on dividends; distributions from a transparent SCSp to partners are generally not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) and the applicable relief declaration to the Luxembourg paying agent before payment. Reduced or zero rates require a completed self-declaration; if tax was withheld, an early refund may be claimed via Form 12/Form 18 with the Luxembourg direct tax administration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% statutory Luxembourg WHT. Royalties: 20% statutory WHT, generally reduced to 0-10% under an applicable double tax treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: Luxembourg entity annual net turnover exceeding EUR 10 million with related-party transactions; Master File: group consolidated annual revenue exceeding EUR 50 million; Country-by-Country Report: group consolidated revenue EUR 750 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain formal Economic Substance Regulations comparable to offshore jurisdictions, but the GAAR, CFC rules and jurisprudence require real economic substance. An SCSp with no Luxembourg office, management, or decision-making substance may be re-characterized as an abusive shell and stripped of treaty/domestic tax benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting craft-beer sales revenue, inflating purchase costs, or submitting forged documentation in the Form 100 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 10,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil reassessment with penalty up to 10% and 0.6% monthly late interest on the unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for taxes, penalties and interest; travel bans and imprisonment can be ordered in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling hazy IPA kegs to an affiliated foreign distributor at artificially low margins or paying excessive royalties to an offshore IP holder to erode Luxembourg profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income to the arm's length standard; penalty between 10% and 50% of the reassessed profit; loss of double-tax treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize non-commercial intercompany terms can be held jointly liable for the tax deficiency and exposed to asset seizure or personal garnishment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a pure paper SCSp with no real office, no material equipment, no local decision-making and no operational activity in Luxembourg to evade the economic substance and transparency rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the SCSp's legal transparency, retroactive taxation at partner level, denial of participation exemptions, and a 50% penalty for abuse of law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partner directors may be civilly liable for the unpaid tax when the partnership is insolvent, and may face travel restrictions and criminal penalties for fraudulent use of a corporate vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large cash payments from bars and restaurants for craft-beer kegs without conducting client due diligence, maintaining cash ledgers, or reporting suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1 million under the Luxembourg AML law of 2020; statutory liquor distribution license may be revoked; business may be barred from intra-EU keg export.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible general partner directors face personal fines, mandatory travel controls, and imprisonment in flagrant non-compliance where money laundering is established.
